subject: Fit indices for a SEM analysis on imputed dataset

messages.author: a3bd102816365b16
messages.subject: Fit indices for a SEM analysis on imputed dataset
parts:
Greetings,

I am using the runMI function in the semTools package to take care of missing data. I've then run a SEM using lavaan. Here's my code: 

# specifying the model structure
e1ymodel2 <- "
  DICint ~ INDXnewkill 
  INDXnewkill  ~ SCLpanas
  SCLpanas ~ DummyText + DummyImage
"

e1yfit2 <- runMI(e1ymodel2, data = e1y.trim, m = 5, miPackage = "mice", ordered = c("DICint"), fun = "sem")
 
summary(e1yfit2)

anova(e1yfit2, indices = "rmsea")
anova(e1yfit2, indices = "srmr")
anova(e1yfit2, indices = "cfi")

I can get the fit indices for RMSEA and SRMR, but I get the following error when I request the CFI:

Error in (function (..., row.names = NULL, check.rows = FALSE, check.names = TRUE, : arguments imply differing number of rows: 13, 0

Any idea as to why there's an error with CFI but not the others? I also get the error message when I request TLI or NFI. Any advice on how to address this issue? 

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Fit indices for a SEM analysis on imputed dataset
parts: e1yfit2 <- runMI(e1ymodel2, data = e1y.trim, m = 5, miPackage = "mice", ordered = c("DICint"), fun = "sem")
Make sure you make use of the miArgs= argument to let mice() know that DICint is an ordinal variable, so it should be imputed with a proportional odds model (method = "polr").

anova(e1yfit2, indices = "rmsea")
anova(e1yfit2, indices = "srmr")
anova(e1yfit2, indices = "cfi")

FYI, you can put them all in a vector to get all at once (when there is not an error from CFI):

anova(..., indices = c("rmsea","srmr","cfi")
Any idea as to why there's an error with CFI but not the others? I also get the error message when I request TLI or NFI. Any advice on how to address this issue?

Then it sounds like an issue with the baseline model.  I don't have a problem getting incremental fit indices with continuous or categorical data, so could you first check whether the error occurs in the latest development version(s)? (semTools_0.4-15.915 and lavaan_0.6-1.1208)  

If so, the issue might be with the fixed.x= argument (your path analysis has some exogenous variables).  I thought I set this to FALSE internally, but could you try setting fixed.x=FALSE?  If the error persists, I think I would need you to send me an R script and some data to reproduce the problem, in order for me to fix it.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Fit indices for a SEM analysis on imputed dataset
parts: I still get the same error as I did before about arguments implying a different number of rows.

I'm not quite certain when this error occurs (e.g., in semTools or in the mice package, before or after imputation, etc.).  Could you narrow it down by imputing the data first, then passing a list of imputed data sets to runMI?
e1yfit2 <- runMI(e1ymodel2, data = e1y.trim, m = 5, miPackage = "mice", ordered = c("DICint"), fun = "sem", miArgs = list(ords="DICint"), fixed.x = FALSE)

ords= is an argument for the amelia() function, not for the mice() function.  Again, try imputing your data first, to have more control over that process and see whether an error occurs there.  That will also enable you to check your imputations to see if there is anything strange happening that would make results have a different form across imputations.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
